title: Beylik of Aydin
capsule: The Beylik of Aydin (Aydınoğulları) was a Turkic maritime principality established in western Anatolia around 1308, following the fragmentation of the Sultanate of Rum, with capitals at Birgi and Selçuk (Ephesus). Under Mehmed Bey and especially his son Umur Bey (r. c.1334–1348), the beylik became the dominant Aegean naval power, basing its fleet at Smyrna after capturing the city in 1317 and raiding deep into the Byzantine and Latin Aegean; this piracy provoked the Smyrniote Crusades, during which Umur Bey was killed at Smyrna in May 1348. Aydin's independence was temporarily extinguished when Timur crushed the Ottomans at Ankara (1402) and restored the beyliks; it was finally absorbed into the Ottoman Empire in 1426.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The beylik's core territory in the lower Meander valley and Aegean littoral is attested in Byzantine and Ottoman sources, but its fluctuating frontier with neighbouring beyliks is imprecisely bounded.
